![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/e2065775ae6372e8c820b5e2f19f6f105e032dcd37db1e32e04af5bfa6a4faf9.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

I. $x\in (-3,-2]\cup (2,4)$

II. $x\in (0,2]$

III. $x\in [1,4)$
question.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is invertible on the intervals $x\in (-3,-2]\cup (2,4)$ and $x\in (0,2].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/3c5bc724ee29aee7bef2790012bf0e73ce1ed087134213dbad36a670fd136a36.png)

        

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $[1,4)$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14243592/assets/03b9d70513a4ef99b39c9f05d0c0ac803f8e5611d0967015e9c1d9c0f45bd418.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and II only".
